analyses.title: Dialogue Acts, Synchronizing Units, and Anaphora Resolution
analyses.research_question: How can pronouns and demonstratives in spontaneous spoken dialogue be classified and resolved when their antecedents may be noun phrases, sentential discourse material, or not linguistically identifiable?
analyses.methodology: The authors conduct a corpus analysis of spontaneous spoken dialogues and annotate anaphor types, antecedents, and dialogue-act segmentation, including inter-annotator agreement tests. They then develop an anaphora-resolution algorithm, based on Strube's earlier model, that classifies pronouns and demonstratives and links them to nominal or sentential antecedents. Potential antecedent domains are constrained using dialogue acts organized into Synchronizing Units intended to reflect establishment of common ground.

key_findings.finding: Fewer than half of the analyzed pronouns and demonstratives have noun-phrase antecedents in the preceding discourse.
Approximately 22% of the analyzed pronouns and demonstratives have sentential antecedents, showing that proposition-like discourse material is an empirically important antecedent class.
The remaining analyzed pronouns and demonstratives include cases with no identifiable linguistic antecedent.
Inter-annotator agreement experiments for anaphor typing, antecedent identification, and dialogue-act segmentation were reported to support the reliability of the annotation method.
The proposed resolver handles both noun-phrase and sentential antecedents rather than restricting antecedent search to nominal expressions.
Dialogue acts and Synchronizing Units are used to constrain antecedent accessibility by modeling which material has entered conversational common ground.
Predicate information, noun-phrase form, and dialogue structure are reported as useful information sources for anaphora resolution.

limitations: Only the abstract was accessible from the publisher source used here, so dataset size, detailed annotation procedures, agreement coefficients, algorithmic evaluation scores, and error analyses could not be verified from the paper itself.
The study addresses anaphoric reference rather than explicit question-to-reply or proposition-to-reply alignment.
The accessible abstract does not separately analyze partial answers, multiple simultaneous questions, or unanswered questions.
Although sentential antecedents provide evidence for proposition-level reference, the accessible abstract does not establish how often an antecedent spans multiple distinct propositions.
The accessible source does not establish public availability of the authors' annotations or implementation.
raw_claims: Less than half of the examined pronouns and demonstratives have preceding noun-phrase antecedents.
About 22% of the examined anaphoric expressions have sentential antecedents.
Some pronouns and demonstratives have no identifiable linguistic antecedent.
The corpus analysis includes annotation of anaphor types and their antecedents.
Dialogue segmentation into dialogue acts was also subjected to inter-annotator agreement testing.
The authors report that their annotation scheme is reliable enough to serve as a reference standard for evaluating the resolver.
The resolution algorithm can classify pronouns and demonstratives and link them to either noun-phrase or sentential antecedents.
Potential antecedents are constrained using dialogue-act structure.
Synchronizing Units are intended to represent conversational common ground.
Predicate information, noun-phrase form, and dialogue structure are used by the resolution process.
